label: Token-managed automatic liquidity
summary: Execute bounded canonical-pool liquidity operations from token-controlled inventory without changing standard hook callbacks.
requiredFacts: Token-controlled funding source, inventory asset, threshold, cadence, slippage and deadline
Exact router or PoolManager path and observed-balance accounting for every operation
Who triggers, pauses, rescues or reconfigures execution and what happens after failure
LP position owner, fee beneficiary, removal authority and retirement behavior
Separation from standard Programmable fee-hook balances, liabilities and claims
requiredFiles: Token, hook and pool integration tests
requiredTests: Threshold boundaries, repeated triggers and bounded inventory accumulation
Slippage, deadline, zero-liquidity, adverse-price and partial-failure behavior
Observed balance deltas across token, router, PoolManager and LP position
Reentrancy, recursive trigger, sandwich and parameter-authority adversarial cases
Position creation, fee collection, removal, rescue and user-exit lifecycle
risks: Token-controlled swaps can be sandwiched or recursively triggered
Router or PoolManager incompatibility can strand token-owned inventory
Unclear LP custody or rescue authority can redirect user-funded value
